title: Pearl's Ladder of Causation
summary: Pearl's ladder: association works with two bodies (data and patterns), intervention adds causal context, counterfactuals add the ability to imagine alternatives. Each rung adds a body to the coordination stack; the missing causal context is what current AI lacks.
source: Ch02 — "Association works with two bodies. Intervention requires three. Counterfactuals require conscious coordination of all three plus the ability to imagine alternatives."

nodes.label: Intervention
nodes.description: Causal manipulation: "what if I do X?" (rung 2)

nodes.label: Counterfactual
nodes.description: Reasoning about alternatives: "what if I had done X instead?" (rung 3)

nodes.label: Imagination
nodes.description: Capacity to construct and evaluate hypothetical worlds

nodes.label: Causal Context
nodes.description: The causal model of mechanisms that current AI lacks

edges.description: Intervention requires a causal model of mechanisms
Counterfactuals require the same causal model

identifiability_note: Current AI works at rung 1 only. Without the causal context (n5) neither intervention nor counterfactual claims are identifiable from association data; Pearl's do-calculus supplies the structural assumptions.
